source_caption:
To capture the absolute, soul-crushing devastation of a father realizing he has missed the entire lives of his children, Christopher Nolan made a brilliant directorial choice for the film’s most emotionally shattering scene. When Cooper returns from the water planet to discover over two decades have passed and sits down to watch twenty-three years of accumulated video messages, Matthew McConaughey’s agonizing breakdown was captured in a single, intensely intimate take. To guarantee an entirely raw reaction, Nolan purposefully ensured McConaughey had not seen any of the pre-recorded footage of the actors playing his children beforehand. As Cooper helplessly watches his son grow up and eventually give up hope, and his daughter finally reach the exact age he was when he left, the breathless, suffocating sobbing is incredibly real. By completely stripping away the massive sci-fi spectacle to focus entirely on the weeping face of a profoundly broken man, McConaughey masterfully proves that the most paralyzing terror of deep space is not a black hole or a hostile world, but the irreversible, devastating theft of time.

Interstellar (2014), directed by Christopher Nolan, starring Matthew McConaughey, Anne Hathaway, Jessica Chastain. Facing a catastrophic, rapidly approaching global blight that will inevitably destroy humanity, a brilliant former NASA pilot is tasked with leading a desperate, highly dangerous interstellar mission through a newly discovered wormhole to find a habitable new world before time completely runs out on Earth.

source_details.synopsis: Interstellar is a 2014 epic science fiction drama film directed by Christopher Nolan, who co-wrote the screenplay with his brother, Jonathan Nolan. It features an ensemble cast led by Matthew McConaughey, Anne Hathaway, Jessica Chastain, Bill Irwin, Ellen Burstyn, and Michael Caine. Set in a dystopian future where Earth is suffering from catastrophic blight and famine, the film follows a group of astronauts who travel through space in search of a new home for humanity. The film began development in 2006 from a treatment by producer Lynda Obst and theoretical physicist Kip Thorne, and was originally set to be directed by Steven Spielberg.
